ideas.title: Rock the brushes until the sparks die
ideas.critique: Real commutation is a step nobody expected: per-coil L/R reversal against a load-shifted neutral gives a skill with an optimum that moves, and the dusk spark light answers the big goal's moment with physics behind it. The risk is that it turns into a 1D rig of numbers typed in for one motor, and the film would be one more fixed camera on a device running alone unless the hand really turns the holder.

ideas.title: The winch: the drum motor hauls the empty cart up the planks
ideas.critique: This is the first time the motor moves something that matters, and 'hook it to anything, it hauls or stalls by its own torque' is the general version worth having. But 4.35 vs 9.5 cm/s quoted before anything is built smells like a fitted table, and a cart creeping on planks is slow to watch unless stalls and choices are what you see.

ideas.title: Pots that tire
ideas.critique: Concentration polarisation with a diffusion layer and stirring is honest chemistry and an open road step. What you see, though, is a motor slowing over minutes, a sag in a number, which barely reads on film and repeats the pots post.

ideas.title: Crank it backwards: the friends light a wire
ideas.critique: The payoff is a wire glowing until it burns through, which the island already filmed. The motor as a dynamo is a real step, but the friends are animated cranks whose slowdown under load is the only new feel, and that cranking is the friends' reaction more than a player's choice.

ideas.title: Form the lead plates: charge, fizz, rest, again
ideas.critique: Planté forming as layer growth per coulomb, with gassing bubbles once the plate is full, is new chemistry and a visible material change, and it is the cart's battery. As a loop of charge, wait, charge it is a slow grind, and 'darkens each cycle' could easily end up as a lerped colour.

ideas.title: Wind your own coil
ideas.critique: Building the part whose numbers decide the motor is the human's direction itself, and it ties into the big goal. But 'the 2D field table scales with N' is scaling, not solving, and a beak winding turns is a mini task that may end up as a counter with a wire texture.

ideas.title: Stall it and smell the varnish
ideas.critique: A conductor heated by I²R until it fails is the wire post's recipe again, this time on a coil with smoke particles. It only gives a player a choice once there is a winch to overload.

ideas.title: Capstan: friends hold the rope's tail
ideas.critique: Euler's exp(μθ) is a lovely nerdy law, and adding turns so one friend can hold a cart is a satisfying joke. As pitched it is a one-formula rig on a post, and it plays around the cart rather than building it.

ideas.title: The motor in the dark: night shift
ideas.critique: Emitters powered by the simulated power are right for the traced look, but this stacks the commutator and the dynamo and adds only lighting and a gathering of friends. It is a scene to watch with nothing to choose, and the glowing-object-lights-the-ground form has been done.

ideas.title: Brush wear: a ring that grows a groove
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Erosion as a height field on the ring, with feedback into spark energy, is an aging mechanism the island lacks. It needs spark physics that does not exist yet, and filing a ring is upkeep, not play.
